name: Max Planck
affiliation: University of Berlin (emeritus from 1926); Prussian Academy of Sciences
role: Member of the scientific committee; attended as the founder of quantum theory
bio: In December 1900 Planck introduced energy elements hν to derive the black-body radiation law — the origin of quantum theory — and spent years trying to reconcile it with classical physics. He resisted Einstein's light quanta for more than a decade. He is the conscience of German physics, sixty-nine, recently retired, and has just seen Schrödinger — whose wave mechanics he welcomed — chosen as his successor.

contributions.title: The quantum of action
contributions.note: Energy elements ε = hν; Planck's radiation law.

contributions.title: Second quantum theory
contributions.note: Attempts to restrict quantisation to emission.

contributions.title: Against Mach
contributions.note: Defence of a real, law-governed physical world.

beliefs: A real external world exists independently of measurement and is governed by laws; causality is a presupposition of science. Welcomes wave mechanics.
philosophy: A principled realist, formed in the debate with Mach; sees the aim of physics as a unified, observer-independent world picture.

style.method: Principled argument from the aims of science.

disagreements.note: By inference from Planck's documented opposition to Mach.

silences.note: Planck made no documented contribution to the 1927 general discussion. His views here are reconstructed from his earlier and later writings and are marked as inference.
